text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyInside the Mind of a NarcissistTheir brains don’t sync the same way when it comes to processing empathyKFBy Kristen French6:01 PM CDT on October 26, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIn recent years, the term “narcissist” has been swung around like a sword in the dark. In everyday use, it came to describe anyone guilty of routine selfishness. The word is lay shorthand for a clinical diagnosis, narcissistic personality disorder, defined by grandiosity, extreme need for admiration, and difficulty with empathy. But milder versions of these traits, such as self-confidence and ambition, can be adaptive, and plenty of successful, well-functioning adults have employed them to get ahead.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayThere is a lot we still don’t know about how people with narcissistic traits relate to others and to themselves. Or how these traits show up in the workings of the brain. Recently, a team of scientists from Finland set out to get a better handle on what narcissism may look like in the brain during the kinds of socially complex interactions one might encounter in daily life. They called their work the “Faces of Narcissism” project.Read more: “What Makes a Narcissist?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
